---
title: "Geospatial diversity workflows"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  dpi = 150,
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(tidydiversity)
library(tidymapr)
```

tidymapr and tidydiversity share one tidy pipeline, in the same way dplyr
and ggplot2 do: tidydiversity estimates diversity, tidymapr puts it on a
map. This article covers study-site maps for papers, sites as `sf` tables,
rasters joined as columns, occurrence cleaning, distances for
`tidydiversity::beta_decay()`, Hill numbers on maps, stem maps over
topography, WorldClim/CHELSA bioclim (including CMIP6), tidy SDMs
(`sdm_*`) and Moran's I for spatial autocorrelation. Hand off to **tmap**
or **leaflet** with `as_sf()` / `as_spat_raster()` when you want
interactive maps; those stay Suggests only. Diversity, stem and modelling
verbs (`div_*`, `beta_*`, `stems_*`, `model_*`, `plot_partial()`) come from
tidydiversity.

## Study-site map (publication figure)

Papers almost always need a map of the sampling sites. The Papua New Guinea
example tables (`png_ants`, `png_frogs`, `png_tree_ants`) record elevation
but not GPS, so [geo_example_sites()] supplies illustrative WGS84 positions
near Mt Wilhelm and the Wanang canopy plots. Replace them with your own GPS
before publication.

```{r study-sites-map, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.2, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
sites <- geo_example_sites("wilhelm")
# Keep the five elevations shared by both seasons in png_ants
sites <- sites[sites$elevation <= 2200, ]
sites$season <- "both"

plot_sites(
  sites,
  lon,
  lat,
  colour = elevation_band,
  label = site,
  scale_bar = TRUE,
  north_arrow = TRUE
) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Study sites along Mt Wilhelm, Papua New Guinea",
    subtitle = "Illustrative coordinates for the elevational gradient"
  )
```

Join the same coordinates to community data when you need a map per season
or taxon:

```{r study-sites-facet, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.2, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
ants <- unique(png_ants[c("site", "elevation", "season")])
ants <- dplyr::left_join(ants, sites[c("site", "lon", "lat")], by = "site")
plot_sites(
  ants,
  lon,
  lat,
  colour = elevation,
  facet = season,
  label = site
) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "PNG ant bait sites by season")
```

## Sites and rasters

```{r sites}
sites <- geo_example_sites("wilhelm")
sites <- sites[sites$elevation <= 2200, ]
sf_sites <- geo_as_sf(sites, lon, lat, site = site)
sf_sites
```

```{r extract, eval = requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)}
# Demo raster in place of CHELSA / WorldClim / SRTM
r <- terra::rast(
  ncols = 40, nrows = 40,
  xmin = 144.8, xmax = 145.5, ymin = -6.0, ymax = -5.5,
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)
terra::values(r) <- sites$elevation[1] +
  800 * (terra::yFromCell(r, seq_len(terra::ncell(r))) + 6)
names(r) <- "elev_proxy"
sites_x <- geo_extract(sites, r, lon, lat)
sites_x
```

## Clean occurrence records

```{r clean}
occ <- tibble::tibble(
  species = c("Camponotus_sp1", "Camponotus_sp1", "Polyrhachis_sp2",
              "Pheidole_sp3", "ghost"),
  lon = c(145.23, 145.23, 145.12, 0, 12.58),
  lat = c(-5.72, -5.72, -5.78, 0, 55.67)
)
geo_clean(occ, lon, lat, species = species, value = "flagged")[
  c("species", "lon", "lat", ".zer", ".gbf", ".dpl", ".summary")
]
```

`geo_gbif()` accepts a pre-downloaded GBIF table (or downloads with
**rgbif** when installed) and pipes into the same cleaner.

## Distance decay with tidydiversity

```{r decay}
com <- dplyr::left_join(
  png_ants,
  sites[c("site", "lon", "lat")],
  by = "site"
)
decay_geo <- geo_decay(com, lon, lat, .by = season, method = "haversine")
decay_elev <- geo_decay(
  com, elevation = elevation, .by = season, method = "elevation"
)
head(decay_geo)
```

```{r decay-plot, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
ggplot2::autoplot(decay_geo) + ggplot2::labs(title = "Geographic distance decay")
```

## Map Hill numbers

```{r map, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
est <- div_estimate(png_ants, q = 0, nboot = 0, .by = season)
est <- dplyr::left_join(est, sites[c("site", "lon", "lat")], by = "site")
est_dry <- est[est$season == "dry", ]
plot_geo(est_dry, estimate, lon, lat, label = site) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Observed richness of PNG ants (dry season)")
```

## Spatial autocorrelation

```{r moran}
set.seed(1)
g <- expand.grid(x = 1:8, y = 1:8)
g$richness <- g$x + g$y + 0.05 * stats::rnorm(nrow(g))
geo_moran(g, richness, lon = x, lat = y, nperm = 199, correlogram = TRUE)
```


## Basemaps

`plot_sites()` and `plot_geo()` take a `basemap` argument. Use `"coast"`
offline, online tile names (`"osm"`, `"carto"`, `"carto_dark"`, `"esri"`)
when connected, or pass a `SpatRaster` / file path. Tile fetch failures fall
back to the coast basemap with a message. Scale bar and north arrow stay on.

```{r basemap-coast, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
sites <- geo_example_sites("wilhelm")
sites <- sites[sites$elevation <= 2200, ]
plot_sites(
  sites, lon, lat,
  colour = elevation_band,
  label = site,
  basemap = "coast"
) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Study sites with a coast basemap")
```

## Vector and raster analysis

Buffer sites, then summarise a raster inside each buffer (for example mean
elevation). Crop and mask keep the analysis inside the study area.

```{r buffer-zonal, eval = requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
sites_sf <- geo_as_sf(sites, lon, lat)
buf <- geo_buffer(sites_sf, dist = 5000)
r <- terra::rast(
  ncols = 40, nrows = 40,
  xmin = 144.8, xmax = 145.5, ymin = -6.0, ymax = -5.5,
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)
terra::values(r) <- sites$elevation[1] +
  800 * (terra::yFromCell(r, seq_len(terra::ncell(r))) + 6)
names(r) <- "elev_proxy"
geo_raster_zonal(r, buf, fun = "mean")
cropped <- geo_raster_crop(r, buf)
masked <- geo_raster_mask(r, buf)
c(ncell_full = terra::ncell(r), ncell_crop = terra::ncell(cropped))
```

## Bioclimatic variables (WorldClim and CHELSA)

Biodiversity models often need temperature and rainfall surfaces. List the
19 bioclim variables with [geo_bioclim_vars()], then read or download them
with [geo_worldclim()] or [geo_chelsa()] (or the front door [geo_bioclim()]).
Pass `path` for local GeoTIFFs when offline. Cite the data sources in any
paper that uses them: WorldClim 2 (Fick and Hijmans 2017, CC BY 4.0) and
CHELSA (Karger et al. 2017, CC BY 4.0).

```{r bioclim-vars}
geo_bioclim_vars()[c(1, 12), ]
```

```{r bioclim-extract, eval = requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
# Offline demo: a local stand-in for bio1 joined to sites
bio1 <- terra::rast(
  ncols = 20, nrows = 20,
  xmin = 144.8, xmax = 145.5, ymin = -6.0, ymax = -5.5,
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)
terra::values(bio1) <- 22
names(bio1) <- "bio1"
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
terra::writeRaster(bio1, tmp, overwrite = TRUE)
clim <- geo_worldclim(vars = "bio1", path = tmp, download = FALSE)
geo_extract(sites, clim, lon, lat)
```

## Tree stems over topography (ForestGEO / Wanang)

Large forest dynamics plots map every stem in local metre coordinates
(`gx`, `gy`) over a DEM. [plot_topo()] draws stems with contour lines and
hillshade, coloured by species and sized by DBH. The package does not yet
ship real Wanang stem coordinates; [geo_example_stems()] and
[geo_example_dem()] give an illustrative 100 m x 100 m plot in the
ForestGEO column layout. Replace them with your inventory for publication.
ForestGEO / Wanang background: Anderson-Teixeira et al. (2015),
doi:10.1111/gcb.12712; ForestGEO <https://forestgeo.si.edu/>.

```{r topo-stems, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 5.5, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)}
stems <- geo_example_stems()
dem <- geo_example_dem()
plot_topo(
  stems,
  colour = species,
  size = dbh,
  dem = dem,
  boundary = c(0, 0, 100, 100)
) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Stem map over topography",
    subtitle = "Illustrative ForestGEO-style plot (replace with real gx, gy, DEM)"
  )
```

## ForestGEO-style plots

Forest dynamics plots (ForestGEO / CTFS) map every stem in local metres and
repeat the census about every five years (Condit 1998; Anderson-Teixeira
et al. 2015). tidymapr handles the spatial steps and tidydiversity the census
summaries:

1. `tidydiversity::stems_as_trees()` picks the main stem per tree.
2. [stems_quadrat()] assigns 20 m x 20 m quadrats from `gx` / `gy`.
3. `tidydiversity::stems_abundance()` and `tidydiversity::stems_basal_area()` summarise counts and
   basal area (`pi/4 * dbh^2`).
4. `tidydiversity::stems_size_class()` bins DBH.
5. `tidydiversity::stems_demography()` estimates mortality, recruitment and growth between
   two censuses.
6. [stems_habitat()] joins quadrat topography or habitat,
   [stems_neighbours()] counts neighbours within a radius and
   [stems_habitat_test()] runs the torus-translation habitat test.
7. `tidydiversity::stems_as_community()` feeds `tidydiversity::div_hill()` and friends.
8. [plot_topo()] maps stems on hillshade and contours.

```{r forestgeo-demo, eval = requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)}
stems <- geo_example_stems()
stems_basal_area(stems, dbh_unit = "mm", .by = species)
cens <- geo_example_censuses()
stems_demography(cens$census1, cens$census2, time = 5, dbh_unit = "mm")
com <- stems_as_community(stems_quadrat(stems))
div_hill(com, q = c(0, 1, 2))
```


## Environmental distance decay

After joining bioclim columns with [geo_extract()] / [geo_bioclim()], pass
`method = "environmental"` to [geo_distance()] or [geo_decay()] to get
Euclidean (scaled) or Gower distances among sites. The result feeds
`tidydiversity::beta_decay_model()` the same way as geographic or elevational distance.

```{r env-decay, eval = requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
sites <- unique(png_ants[c("site", "elevation", "season")])
sites$lon <- 145.0 + sites$elevation / 1e5
sites$lat <- -5.8 - sites$elevation / 2e5
sites$bio1 <- 25 - sites$elevation / 400
com <- dplyr::left_join(
  dplyr::filter(png_ants, season == "wet"),
  sites[c("site", "season", "lon", "lat", "bio1")],
  by = c("site", "season")
)
decay <- geo_decay(com, lon, lat, method = "environmental", vars = "bio1")
head(decay)
```

## Spatial eigenvectors, rarefaction and grain

[geo_mem()] builds dbMEM / PCNM eigenvectors from site coordinates.
[geo_rarefy_spatial()] accumulates richness by distance from a seed sample.
[geo_grain()] rebins sites into square cells of several sizes and recomputes
Hill numbers, so MAUP / grain effects are visible. [geo_middomain()] adds a
geometric mid-domain null for elevational richness.

```{r spatial-helpers}
g <- expand.grid(lon = 1:5, lat = 1:4)
g$site <- paste0("s", seq_len(nrow(g)))
names(geo_mem(g, lon, lat, site = site, method = "euclidean"))[1:6]
```

## Tidy species distribution models

[sdm_fit()], [sdm_predict()], [sdm_evaluate()] and [plot_sdm()] provide a
tidyverse-style SDM workflow. Engines: `"glm"`, `"gam"` (mgcv) and a native
`"maxnet"`-like presence-background model with linear and quadratic features
(no Java Maxent, no biomod2 or dismo). Predictors may be columns or a
SpatRaster from [geo_bioclim()].

```{r sdm-demo, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4.5, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
set.seed(1)
grid <- expand.grid(
  lon = seq(145, 145.5, length.out = 20),
  lat = seq(-5.9, -5.5, length.out = 16)
)
grid$bio1 <- 15 + 12 * (grid$lat - min(grid$lat)) / diff(range(grid$lat))
pa <- grid
pa$present <- as.integer(pa$bio1 > 22)
fit <- sdm_fit(pa, predictors = "bio1", present = present, engine = "glm")
sdm_evaluate(fit)
plot_sdm(sdm_predict(fit, newdata = grid)) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "SDM suitability (demonstration)",
    subtitle = "Simulated species present only at high bio1"
  )
```

## Elevation, future climate and planning export

[geo_elevation()] downloads or reads an SRTM-style DEM (geodata / elevatr,
with offline `path`). [geo_chelsa()] accepts `scenario` and `year` for
CHELSA-CMIP6 future layers (Karger et al. 2023; skip network with
`download = FALSE` on CRAN). [geo_as_features()] exports a site-by-feature
matrix for prioritizr; spectral / Google Earth Engine helpers remain
deferred.


## Partial-effect and surface plots (Moses et al. 2021)

The Mt Wilhelm litter-ant analysis in Moses et al. (2021,
doi:10.1111/btp.12914) fitted Poisson and negative-binomial GLMs for
richness and abundance against elevation and litter depth, then used
**visreg** (`visreg2d`) for the interaction surface and hand-converted the
result to ggplot. tidydiversity replaces that jump with `tidydiversity::model_count()`,
`tidydiversity::plot_partial()` and `tidydiversity::plot_surface()` in one tidy workflow (no visreg,
plotmo or aods3).

```{r moses-partial, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
ants <- png_ants |>
  dplyr::group_by(site, elevation) |>
  dplyr::summarise(richness = dplyr::n_distinct(species), .groups = "drop")
set.seed(1)
ants$litter <- 1 + ants$elevation / 2000 + stats::rnorm(nrow(ants), 0, 0.25)
fit <- model_count(
  ants, richness ~ elevation * litter, family = "poisson"
)
plot_partial(fit, elevation, residuals = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Partial effect of elevation on richness")
plot_surface(fit, elevation, litter) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Elevation x litter surface",
    subtitle = "Pattern after Moses et al. 2021; illustrative litter values"
  )
```


## GADM boundaries and GDAL-backed I/O

Administrative backdrops come from [GADM](https://gadm.org) via
[geo_gadm()]. Level 0 is the country outline, level 1 provinces, level 2
districts. Downloads are cached under
`tools::R_user_dir("tidymapr", "cache")/gadm` and are **not** bundled
in the package. GADM is free for academic use; redistribution of the full
database is restricted ([license](https://gadm.org/license.html)). Set
`download = FALSE` on CRAN or offline runners, or pass a local GeoPackage
with `path`.

```{r gadm, eval = FALSE}
# Online once (needs geodata + network):
png_prov <- geo_gadm("PNG", level = 1)
plot_sites(
  geo_example_sites("wilhelm"), lon, lat,
  colour = elevation_band, admin = png_prov, inset = "png"
)
# Clip a raster to the country outline (GDAL warp via terra):
# dem <- geo_raster_mask(dem, geo_gadm("PNG", level = 0))
```

Raster and vector files are read and written through **GDAL** (via terra and
sf). Prefer [geo_read()] / [geo_write()] (and the vector/raster twins) over
calling `st_read`, `rast`, `gdal_translate`, or the retired **rgdal** package.
Format is taken from the file extension; see `?geo_read` for the full table
(GeoTIFF/COG, NetCDF, ASCII grid, GeoPackage, shapefile, GeoJSON, KML/KMZ,
GML, FileGDB when available, CSV lon/lat occurrence tables).

```{r gdal-io, eval = FALSE}
r <- geo_read("elevation.tif")
geo_write(geo_raster_project(r, "EPSG:32755"), "elev_utm55s.tif", overwrite = TRUE)
pts <- geo_read("sites.gpkg")
geo_write(as_sf(geo_example_sites("wilhelm")), "sites.gpkg", overwrite = TRUE)
occ <- geo_read("occurrences.csv")  # lon/lat columns -> sf
```

Save map figures from `plot_sites()` / `plot_geo()` / `plot_sdm()` /
`plot_topo()` with [geo_save()] (or `tidydiversity::plot_save()` for journal column sizes):

```{r geo-save, eval = FALSE}
p <- plot_sites(
  geo_example_sites("wilhelm"), lon, lat,
  colour = elevation_band, inset = "png", basemap = "esri"
)
geo_save(p, "wilhelm_sites.png", width = 180, height = 140, units = "mm", dpi = 300)
geo_save(p, "wilhelm_sites.pdf")
```

## Legends, insets and hand-off to tmap / leaflet

`plot_sites()`, `plot_geo()` and `plot_sdm()` draw ggplot maps with
collision-aware placement of the scale bar, north arrow, inside legend and
optional overview inset (the emptiest panel corner wins, so decorations do
not sit on sites). Legends support a title, inside/outside position, a frame,
ordered keys, and combined colour + size (for example a Hill number with
elevation). Set `inset = "png"` or `inset = TRUE` for a Papua New Guinea /
auto locator map with the main extent marked.

```{r map-legend-inset, eval = FALSE}
sites <- geo_example_sites("wilhelm")
plot_sites(
  sites, lon, lat,
  colour = elevation_band, size = elevation, label = site,
  legend_title = "Elevation band",
  legend_position = "auto",
  legend_frame = TRUE,
  inset = "png",
  basemap = "esri"
)
```

[as_sf()] and [as_spat_raster()] return plain **sf** / **terra** objects with
a CRS so the same sites hand off to **tmap** (legends via `tm_dots()` /
`tm_layout()`, overview via `tm_inset()`) or **leaflet**. Those packages stay
Suggests only.

```{r tmap-leaflet, eval = FALSE}
sites <- geo_example_sites("wilhelm")
pts <- as_sf(sites)

if (requireNamespace("tmap", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # tmap v3/v4: col/size legends, compass, scale bar, inset overview
  bb_png <- c(xmin = 140.5, ymin = -12, xmax = 156.5, ymax = -1)
  tmap::tm_shape(pts) +
    tmap::tm_dots(col = "elevation", size = 0.3) +
    tmap::tm_layout(legend.outside = FALSE, legend.frame = TRUE) +
    tmap::tm_compass(position = c("right", "top")) +
    tmap::tm_scale_bar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
    tmap::tm_inset(tmap::tm_shape(pts) + tmap::tm_dots(),
                   position = c("left", "top"))
}
if (requireNamespace("leaflet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  leaflet::leaflet(pts) |>
    leaflet::addTiles() |>
    leaflet::addCircleMarkers(popup = ~site)
}
```
